tariff_period_stats.title: Statistics per tariff period
tariff_period_stats.description:
Gives every import period its own kWh and cost statistics, so the Energy dashboard can draw each period as its own grid source in its own colour. Turning this on works out your whole stored history, which can take a minute. The combined statistics are not changed.

**To use them:**
1. In Settings > Dashboards > Energy, add one grid consumption source per period below. For each, pick its kWh statistic and, under cost, choose "Use an entity tracking the total costs" and pick the matching cost statistic.
2. Remove your combined grid source (or turn off its cost). Using it alongside these sources counts your energy and cost twice.
3. Home Assistant does not apply its own daily cost adjustment to sources set up this way, so leave the daily cost adjustment at 0 on every one of them. By default these costs leave out the daily supply charge. If your tariff has more than one period, the next step lets you put the supply charge into the period costs instead. To see your full cost including the supply charge without that, use the combined cost statistic (not these sources).

{details}

Renaming or removing a period stops its statistics being written but leaves the old ones in place; clear them in Developer Tools > Statistics if you no longer want them. Turning this off keeps everything already written.

data.enabled: Record statistics for each tariff period

tariff_supply_mode.title: Supply charge in period costs
tariff_supply_mode.description:
Home Assistant does not apply its daily cost adjustment to the period sources, so the daily supply charge ({daily_supply}) does not reach the dashboard unless it is built into the period costs. Choose where it goes. Leave the daily cost adjustment in the Energy dashboard at 0 either way.

**Left out:** the period costs are only usage times rate, and the supply charge is not shown. The combined cost statistic (not these sources) still has your full cost.

**Spread over the day:** every hour carries an equal share of the supply charge, so the period costs add up to your full daily cost and the hourly chart stays smooth.

**On the first hour of the day:** the whole supply charge lands on the first hour of each day, in whichever period covers it. The totals match your full cost, with a step at that hour.

With either of the last two, a period's cost divided by its kWh reads higher than its tariff rate, because it includes part of the supply charge.

If you change the choice, leave the box ticked to rewrite the recorded period costs now (this can take a minute). If you untick it, the choice is saved but older days keep their old costs until you run "Recalculate cost history".

tariff_recalculate.title: Recalculate cost history
tariff_recalculate.description: Rewrites the recorded cost for every day from this date using the rates now saved, working from the readings Home Assistant has already stored. Use it after correcting a rate that applied to past days.

tariff_timezone_changed.title: Pricing clock changed
tariff_timezone_changed.description:
You changed the pricing clock from {old_clock} to {new_clock}. The clock moves every time window and the edges of every day, so costs already recorded no longer match your rates.

Leave the box ticked to recalculate all recorded costs now, from the readings Home Assistant holds (this can take a minute). If you untick it the tariff is still saved, but older days keep their old costs until you run "Recalculate cost history".
